sentences.en: Hi, can I ask you guys something?

sentences.en: Last week, producer Lena Richards went to Central Park to ask runners a question.
sentences.zh: 上周，制片人莉娜·理查兹去了中央公园，问了跑步者一个问题。

sentences.en: You need a question?
sentences.zh: 你需要一个问题？

sentences.en: I do.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: What are you listening to?

sentences.en: Everyone's preparing for the marathon and I'm stopping that.
sentences.zh: 大家都在为马拉松做准备，而我却在打断他们。

sentences.en: Yes, my 25th.
sentences.zh: 是的，这是我的第25次。

sentences.en: Your 25th marathon.

sentences.en: Can I ask what you're listening to?

sentences.en: Oh, it's Tony Bennett with Nora Jones.

sentences.zh: 他们的回答是……

sentences.en: This is it.
sentences.zh: 就是这个。

sentences.zh: 《蓝色天堂》。

sentences.en: All very different.
sentences.zh: 都非常不同。

sentences.en: I am listening to The Strokes.
sentences.zh: 我在听The Strokes乐队的歌。

sentences.en: Why are Sundays so depressing?
sentences.zh: 为什么周日总是这么令人沮丧？

sentences.en: Radiohead.
sentences.zh: 电台司令乐队。

sentences.en: Optimistic.
sentences.zh: 《乐观主义者》。

sentences.en: Believe it or not, bad religion.

sentences.en: Their Christmas album.

sentences.en: Jimmy Eat World.
sentences.zh: Jimmy Eat World乐队。

sentences.en: Why do I know the name, but the little girl, you're in the...
sentences.zh: 为什么我知道这个名字，但是那个小女孩，你在……

sentences.en: Middle, the middle, there you go.
sentences.zh: 中间，中间，对了。

sentences.en: Eric Thomas.
sentences.zh: 埃里克·托马斯。

sentences.en: You might be smarter, your family might come from privilege, your daddy might own the company, but you will not outwork me.
sentences.zh: 你可能更聪明，你的家庭可能出身优越，你爸爸可能拥有这家公司，但你绝对不会比我更努力。

sentences.en: He's not a musician, he's like a motivational guy.
sentences.zh: 他不是音乐家，他是个励志演说家。

sentences.en: Eric Thomas.
sentences.zh: 埃里克·托马斯。

sentences.en: Keep the fence.
sentences.zh: 守住防线。

sentences.en: Keep me moving, right?
sentences.zh: 让我保持动力，对吧？

sentences.en: Yeah, they'll take his words and like chop him up and put a beat behind it, you know?
sentences.zh: 是的，他们会截取他的话，配上节奏，你知道吗？

sentences.en: Some of you need to give up your cell phone.
sentences.zh: 你们有些人需要放下手机。

sentences.en: It is not surprising that people like to listen to music while they run.
sentences.zh: 人们喜欢在跑步时听音乐，这并不奇怪。

sentences.en: And for the most part, people told us that it basically just takes the edge off.
sentences.zh: 大多数情况下，人们告诉我们，这基本上能缓解压力。

sentences.en: It just relaxes me.
sentences.zh: 它让我放松。

sentences.en: It helps him set the pace.
sentences.zh: 它能帮他设定节奏。

sentences.en: It's just like a fast running mix.
sentences.zh: 这就像一个快节奏的跑步混音带。

sentences.en: Just like fast BPMs, no, just to help me like feel motivated.
sentences.zh: 就是快节奏的BPM，不，只是为了帮我感觉更有动力。

sentences.en: So I had to sort the BPMs from like the slowest songs to the fastest songs at the end of my run so I'd save my energy towards the end.
sentences.zh: 所以我不得不把BPM从最慢的歌排到最快的歌，放在跑步的最后，这样我就可以在最后保留体力。

sentences.en: Makes things more fun.
sentences.zh: 让事情变得更有趣。

sentences.en: I probably look like a weirdo sometimes because I'm going crazy to my music.
sentences.zh: 我有时看起来可能像个怪人，因为我听着音乐会变得很疯狂。

sentences.en: Or it helps them pretend, maybe just for a minute, that they actually aren't running.
sentences.zh: 或者这能帮助他们假装，哪怕只有一分钟，他们其实并没有在跑步。

sentences.en: Anything to really distract me from like where you're at in the run.
sentences.zh: 任何能真正让我分心，不去想跑步进度的事情。

sentences.en: I guess it just gives me something to think about that's not running.
sentences.zh: 我想这只是给了我一些除了跑步以外可以思考的东西。

sentences.en: But Ben Ratliff, a former New York Times music critic and author, thinks of running to music completely differently.
sentences.zh: 但前《纽约时报》音乐评论家兼作家本·拉特利夫对跑步听音乐的看法完全不同。

sentences.en: He runs to make the music better, not the other way around.
sentences.zh: 他是为了让音乐变得更好而跑步，而不是反过来。

sentences.en: And the fact that he could do that was such a profound discovery to him that he wrote an entire book about it.
sentences.zh: 事实上，他能做到这一点对他来说是一个如此深刻的发现，以至于他为此写了一整本书。

sentences.en: It's called Run the Song.
sentences.zh: 书名叫《Run the Song》。

sentences.en: And so today, on the day of the New York City Marathon, my conversation with Ben Ratliff on how running can make you a better listener.
sentences.zh: 所以今天，在纽约马拉松赛当天，我和本·拉特利夫聊聊跑步如何让你成为一个更好的倾听者。

sentences.en: Hey, I'm Benjamin Poulin.
sentences.zh: 嘿，我是本杰明·普兰。

sentences.en: And I'm Mark Ronson.
sentences.zh: 我是马克·朗森。

sentences.en: And welcome to The Reframers, a podcast that's all about the love of design and the culture that surrounds it.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听《重构者》，这是一个关于设计之爱及其周边文化的播客。

sentences.en: Even back when I was DJing in nightclubs, in the era of vinyl, every night you took 300 of your most prized possessions to work with you,
sentences.zh: 即使在我还在夜店当DJ的黑胶唱片时代，你每天晚上都要带着300件你最珍贵的宝贝去上班，

sentences.en: and you turned a DJ booth into this, like, living pop-up museum of beautiful 50-year-old artifacts.
sentences.zh: 你把DJ台变成了一个活生生的、充满50年历史精美文物的快闪博物馆。

sentences.en: Listen to The Reframers from Audemars Piguet now on your favorite podcast platforMs.
sentences.zh: 现在就在你最喜欢的播客平台上收听爱彼出品的《重构者》。

sentences.en: I'm Wynna Liu.
sentences.zh: 我是刘云娜。

sentences.zh: 我负责编写《纽约时报》游戏中的《Connections》拼图。

sentences.en: And I love horror movies.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢恐怖电影。

sentences.en: I love my dog.
sentences.zh: 我爱我的狗。

sentences.en: And I love trying to trick you.
sentences.zh: 我还喜欢尝试捉弄你们。

sentences.en: I'm Sam Mazursky, and I create the game Spelling Bee and Letterboxd on a daily basis.
sentences.zh: 我是萨姆·马祖斯基，我每天负责制作《Spelling Bee》和《Letterboxd》游戏。

sentences.en: And I have this thing called promesthesia.
sentences.zh: 我有一种叫做“联觉”的东西。

sentences.zh: 我听音乐时能看到颜色。

sentences.en: Ben Ratliff, thank you so much for coming to the Sunday Daily.
sentences.zh: 本·拉特利夫，非常感谢你来到《周日每日新闻》。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: So we are here to talk about running and music, two things which I think a lot of people think go together.
sentences.zh: 我们今天来谈谈跑步和音乐，我认为很多人觉得这两者是绝配。

sentences.en: First, I want to talk a little bit about the backstory to what brings you in here today.
sentences.zh: 首先，我想聊聊今天请你来的背景故事。

sentences.en: You are a longtime music critic.
sentences.zh: 你是一位资深音乐评论家。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Including for the New York Times.
sentences.zh: 包括为《纽约时报》撰稿。

sentences.en: So how did you get into that to begin with?
sentences.zh: 那么你最初是怎么入行的呢？

sentences.en: I saw Miles Davis when I was a teenager.
sentences.zh: 我十几岁时看了迈尔斯·戴维斯的演出。

sentences.en: And I had so much to say about it afterwards that the only response that made sense to me was writing.
sentences.zh: 之后我有太多感触想表达，唯一合理的反应就是写下来。

sentences.en: So I wrote an article for the high school newspaper.
sentences.zh: 所以我为高中校报写了一篇文章。

sentences.en: He did the things that people all know that he did, which was play very short melodic phrases on his trumpet and then leave long silences and just sort of wander around the stage
sentences.zh: 他做了人们都知道他会做的事，就是用小号吹奏非常短的旋律片段，然后留下长时间的沉默，在舞台上四处走动，

sentences.en: and sometimes turn his back to the audience for long periods of time and put like a hole open, the heel of his hand down on a keyboard.
sentences.zh: 有时会长时间背对着观众，把手掌根部压在键盘上。

sentences.en: He just mashed his hand on the keyboard?
sentences.zh: 他只是把手砸在键盘上？

sentences.en: Is that what you're describing?
sentences.zh: 这就是你在描述的吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, to get one of those strange chords.
sentences.zh: 是的，为了得到那种奇怪的和弦。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: And I thought, I don't know what's happening here.
sentences.zh: 我想，我不知道这里发生了什么。

sentences.en: It was so mysterious.
sentences.zh: 太神秘了。

sentences.en: Did you like it, though?
sentences.zh: 不过你喜欢吗？

sentences.en: Like, did you like what you heard?
sentences.zh: 就是说，你喜欢你听到的吗？

sentences.en: Loved it.
sentences.zh: 非常喜欢。

sentences.en: Loved it.
sentences.zh: 非常喜欢。

sentences.en: So tell me about kind of going from there to actually doing criticism professionally.
sentences.zh: 那么告诉我你是如何从那时起开始专业从事评论工作的。

sentences.en: I took one writing class in college with a writer I really admired, the jazz critic for the Village Voice at that time, Gary Giddens.
sentences.zh: 我在大学里上过一门写作课，老师是我非常钦佩的作家，当时《乡村之声》的爵士乐评论家加里·吉登斯。

sentences.en: And this sort of set me on my way.
sentences.zh: 这开启了我的职业道路。

sentences.en: I mean, I just started pitching things to little magazines and getting a job doing it professionally was something I never dreamed would happen.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我开始向小杂志投稿，能以这个为职业是我从未梦想过会发生的事情。

sentences.en: And I couldn't believe that the New York Times was trusting me to choose to write about whatever I wanted to, because that really was what it was like when I started.
sentences.zh: 我简直不敢相信《纽约时报》竟然信任我，让我选择写任何我想写的东西，因为我刚开始的时候确实就是这样。

sentences.en: There was great faith in the music critics that we knew our way around the scene and knew what was worth writing about.
sentences.zh: 报社对音乐评论家有极大的信任，相信我们了解这个圈子，知道什么值得写。

sentences.en: And that didn't necessarily mean what was popular.
sentences.zh: 这并不一定意味着什么受欢迎。

sentences.en: It just meant what was interesting to us.
sentences.zh: 只是意味着什么对我们来说是有趣的。

sentences.en: I wonder if there's a show that stood out to you where you were like, I can't believe I get to do this for a living.
sentences.zh: 我想知道有没有哪场演出让你印象深刻，让你觉得“我真不敢相信我能以此为生”。

sentences.en: I would say that there were some nights at, the Village Vanguard was a club that I went to a lot.
sentences.zh: 我想在“乡村先锋”俱乐部有一些夜晚，那是我经常去的地方。

sentences.en: Still around, I think.
sentences.zh: 我想它现在还在。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: It's been around for 91 years, I think.
sentences.zh: 我想它已经存在91年了。

sentences.en: I saw many, many things there.
sentences.zh: 我在那里看过很多很多演出。

sentences.en: Because you're below the ground, it's a little bit like the experience of being in an airplane, where you're just like, you're in some other sphere.
sentences.zh: 因为你在地下，这有点像在飞机上的体验，你就像是在另一个领域。

sentences.en: And the concerns of what's happening on the planet Earth seem far away.
sentences.zh: 地球上发生的事情似乎都很遥远。

sentences.en: I saw so many groups perform at the Village Vanguard and reach a moment in this improvised music where you as a listener actually didn't know what was going on.
sentences.zh: 我在“乡村先锋”看过很多乐队表演，在即兴音乐中达到一个时刻，作为听众的你实际上不知道发生了什么。

sentences.en: And I loved that feeling.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢那种感觉。

sentences.en: I loved the feeling of getting loSt.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢那种迷失的感觉。

sentences.en: I think about that a lot.
sentences.zh: 我经常想到这一点。

sentences.en: You know, you're describing a job that I think a lot of people would consider like a dream job, right?
sentences.zh: 你知道，你描述的工作，我想很多人会认为是梦想工作，对吧？

sentences.en: Getting to go listen to music, see music, and write about it.
sentences.zh: 可以去听音乐、看演出，并写下评论。

sentences.en: It was.
sentences.zh: 确实是。

sentences.en: It was.
sentences.zh: 确实是。

sentences.en: I mean, I know you don't do that anymore, but I sort of am wondering about that past tense.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我知道你不再做那个了，但我有点好奇你用过去式来描述它。

sentences.en: Like, was there a point that it stopped being what it was at the beginning for you?
sentences.zh: 比如，有没有一个时刻，它不再是你最初感受到的那样了？

sentences.en: No, it always was.
sentences.zh: 不，它一直都是那样。

sentences.en: But after a little while, the opportunities to review performances in the Times grew less and less through editorial decisions that the paper had made.
sentences.zh: 但过了一段时间，由于报社的编辑决策，在《时报》上评论演出的机会越来越少。

sentences.en: And I found myself a little bit at a crossroads because I realized that this was the thing that I loved best, was being at a performance, seeing something happen in real time,
sentences.zh: 我发现自己处于一个十字路口，因为我意识到这是我最热爱的事情，就是在现场，实时看着事情发生，

sentences.en: and using that as a pretext for an essay.
sentences.zh: 并以此作为随笔的借口。

sentences.en: So when I couldn't do it so much anymore,
sentences.zh: 所以当我不能再做那么多的时候，

sentences.en: I think I began to wonder about what comes next.
sentences.zh: 我想我开始思考接下来该做什么。

sentences.en: So you're at this crossroads, and in your book you talk about this moment when you also realized that you were having a hard time even listening to music.
sentences.zh: 所以你处于这个十字路口，在你的书中你谈到了一个时刻，你意识到你甚至很难去听音乐了。

sentences.en: You took a trip to Maine to a recording studio to visit a recording engineer, I believe.
sentences.zh: 你去了缅因州的一家录音室拜访了一位录音工程师，我想是这样。

sentences.en: Yes, that was Bob Ludwig, who people who have spent time looking at the back of record covers will recognize his name because he's been the mastering engineer
sentences.zh: 是的，那是鲍勃·路德维希，花时间看过唱片封底的人都会认出他的名字，因为他是母带工程师，

sentences.en: for thousands of well-known records.
sentences.zh: 为成千上万张知名唱片工作过。

sentences.en: So he has very precise ears, and he put me in his special studio, in his chair where he does his important work, you know, and he put on So What
sentences.zh: 所以他有非常敏锐的耳朵，他把我放在他的特殊工作室里，坐在他做重要工作的那把椅子上，你知道，他放了《So What》

sentences.en: from the Miles Davis record, Kind of Blue.
sentences.zh: 来自迈尔斯·戴维斯的唱片《Kind of Blue》。

sentences.en: And, you know, I know this piece of music really well,
sentences.zh: 你知道，我对这段音乐非常熟悉，

sentences.en: and I wasn't blown away.
sentences.zh: 但我并没有感到震撼。

sentences.en: And you thought you would be?
sentences.zh: 你本以为你会感到震撼吗？

sentences.en: I thought that I was going to get closer to this piece of music than I ever had before, and that didn't happen.
sentences.zh: 我以为我会比以往任何时候都更深入地理解这段音乐，但事实并非如此。

sentences.en: Why did you think you were going to get closer?
sentences.zh: 为什么你觉得你会更深入地理解它？

sentences.en: I thought I was going to get inside it.
sentences.zh: 我以为我会进入它的内部。

sentences.en: Inside it.
sentences.zh: 进入它的内部。

sentences.en: What does that mean?
sentences.zh: 那是什么意思？

sentences.en: Can you translate what that means for a person who maybe isn't super fluent in music?
sentences.zh: 你能为那些对音乐不太精通的人解释一下这是什么意思吗？

sentences.en: Well, audio specialists, audio people, of which I am not one, use the language of space, of atmosphere, to describe how something sounds.
sentences.zh: 嗯，音频专家，或者说音频发烧友——我不是其中一员——他们会用空间和氛围的语言来描述声音听起来如何。

sentences.en: They talk about recorded sound as being like a place that you can inhabit, like a stage almoSt.
sentences.zh: 他们谈论录制的声音时，就像在谈论一个你可以居住的地方，几乎就像一个舞台。

sentences.en: And I thought that I would be able to do this to a degree that had never been possible for me before, and it might be akin to the feeling of actually
sentences.zh: 我以为我能达到一种前所未有的程度，这可能类似于一种感觉，

sentences.en: maybe being in the studio with that group
sentences.zh: 也许就像和那个乐队一起待在录音室里，

sentences.en: in 1959, etc.
sentences.zh: 在1959年等等。

sentences.en: So I was trying to understand if you meant like that you can feel it in your, the music sort of like in your body almost, or you're just talking about like,
sentences.zh: 所以我试图弄清楚你是指你能感觉到它，音乐几乎就在你的身体里，还是说你只是在谈论，

sentences.en: wow, I feel like I'm actually in, this music is so present around me, I feel like I'm actually in the recording studio, like the energy, is it like a...
sentences.zh: 哇，我觉得我真的身临其境，这音乐在我周围如此真实，我觉得我真的在录音室里，那种能量，它就像一个……

sentences.en: No, I think that's a great question.
sentences.zh: 不，我觉得这是一个很好的问题。

sentences.en: I think I meant more of the former, but the idea of the music being inside my body, I suppose I wanted that too.
sentences.zh: 我想我更多是指前者，但关于音乐进入我身体的想法，我想我也想要那种感觉。

sentences.en: And that also wasn't happening.
sentences.zh: 而那也没有发生。

sentences.en: It made me think about that.
sentences.zh: 这让我思考了这个问题。

sentences.en: Like, it also made me realize my desire that, well, what do I want?
sentences.zh: 就像，它也让我意识到我的渴望，嗯，我到底想要什么？

sentences.en: I think I want to be the music, essentially.
sentences.zh: 我想我本质上是想成为音乐本身。

sentences.en: Well, as you said, I want to feel it in my own body.
sentences.zh: 嗯，正如你所说，我想在自己的身体里感受到它。

sentences.en: And this might be different from dancing to it.
sentences.zh: 这可能和伴着音乐跳舞有所不同。

sentences.en: But just so I'm understanding this, the issue here is that you're in this special room, this special chair, you've got all this special audio equipment,
sentences.zh: 但为了确保我理解了，这里的问题在于你身处这个特殊的房间，坐在特殊的椅子上，拥有所有这些特殊的音频设备，

sentences.en: and you're listening to the song, expecting that all of your surroundings are basically going to elevate it.
sentences.zh: 而你正在听这首歌，期待着周围的一切基本上能提升它的体验。

sentences.en: And they didn't.
sentences.zh: 但它们没有。

sentences.en: And that caused you to think, what exactly?
sentences.zh: 那让你想到了什么，确切地说？

sentences.en: I think it just made me feel that I need to figure out a new way of listening.
sentences.zh: 我想这只是让我觉得我需要找到一种新的聆听方式。

sentences.en: And I'm not quite sure what it is.
sentences.zh: 但我不太确定那是什么。

sentences.en: You know, there must be a way to listen better than I have before.
sentences.zh: 你知道，一定有一种比我以前更好的聆听方式。

sentences.en: Weirdly, that was the same weekend that I went running, really, for the first time with a friend of mine.
sentences.zh: 奇怪的是，那正是我第一次和朋友去跑步的那个周末。

sentences.en: And you went running, not trying to seek out some solution.
sentences.zh: 你去跑步了，而不是试图寻找某种解决方案。

sentences.en: No, no, and we certainly weren't listening to music.
sentences.zh: 不，不，我们当然没有听音乐。

sentences.en: There were two unrelated things that happened on the same weekend.
sentences.zh: 那是同一个周末发生的两件无关的事情。

sentences.en: So you leave the session with this engineer,
sentences.zh: 所以你离开了那位工程师的录音室，

sentences.en: unmoved, and perhaps a little bit unmoored by how unmoved you were.
sentences.zh: 无动于衷，甚至可能因为自己的无动于衷而感到有些迷茫。

sentences.en: And you think, I need to figure out a different way to listen to music.
sentences.zh: 然后你心想，我需要找到一种不同的听音乐方式。

sentences.en: And then you go on your first run.
sentences.zh: 接着你就去进行了第一次跑步。

sentences.en: What was that experience like?
sentences.zh: 那次体验如何？

sentences.en: I had memories of running from, you know, being on a high school team or something, and just always hating it.
sentences.zh: 我对跑步有记忆，你知道，来自高中校队之类的经历，我总是很讨厌它。

sentences.en: And thinking,
sentences.zh: 并且心想，

sentences.en: I'm not good at this.
sentences.zh: 我不擅长这个。

sentences.en: I don't see the appeal.
sentences.zh: 我看不出有什么吸引力。

sentences.en: Relatable.
sentences.zh: 深有同感。

sentences.en: It seems like punishment, really.
sentences.zh: 这看起来简直就是惩罚。

sentences.en: Boring, etc.
sentences.zh: 无聊，等等。

sentences.en: And I just thought, well, you know, people can change.
sentences.zh: 我只是想，嗯，你知道，人是可以改变的。

sentences.en: Here I am, an adult.
sentences.zh: 现在的我，已经是个成年人了。

sentences.en: Maybe I'll like it this time.
sentences.zh: 也许这次我会喜欢它。

sentences.en: And I think that's when I realized, oh, okay, this is what I'm going to do every day.
sentences.zh: 我想就在那时我意识到，哦，好吧，这就是我每天要做的事情。

sentences.en: Why?
sentences.zh: 为什么？

sentences.en: What was it about it?
sentences.zh: 它有什么特别之处？

sentences.en: Well, because I felt like a million bucks after I came back every time
sentences.zh: 嗯，因为我每次回来都感觉棒极了，

sentences.en: I thought better, I wrote better, I had crazier thoughts, which I was dying to articulate.
sentences.zh: 我思考得更好，写作得更好，我有更疯狂的想法，我渴望表达出来。

sentences.en: What kind of crazy thoughts?
sentences.zh: 什么样的疯狂想法？

sentences.en: Crazy sentences,
sentences.zh: 疯狂的句子，

sentences.en: crazy syntax, crazy vocabulary.
sentences.zh: 疯狂的句法，疯狂的词汇。

sentences.en: There's this wonderful scene in First Wives Club where Goldie Hawn talks about how exercise gives her the best inspiration.
sentences.zh: 在电影《大老婆俱乐部》里有一个精彩的场景，歌蒂·韩谈到锻炼如何给她最好的灵感。

sentences.en: I tell you, I get my best ideas when I'm working out.
sentences.zh: 我告诉你，我在锻炼时能得到最好的点子。

sentences.en: You, you get ideas.
sentences.zh: 你，你得到了点子。

sentences.en: You're reminding me of that.
sentences.zh: 你让我想起了那个场景。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I think that thinking is one of the greatest parts of running.
sentences.zh: 我认为思考是跑步最棒的部分之一。

sentences.en: And just so I'm clear, during this early period, are you still not listening to music after this initial time?
sentences.zh: 为了明确一下，在这一早期阶段，在最初那次之后，你还是没有听音乐吗？

sentences.en: No, not really.
sentences.zh: 不，并没有。

sentences.en: I didn't have the setup for it.
sentences.zh: 我没有相应的设备。

sentences.en: I wasn't even sure how to do it.
sentences.zh: 我甚至不确定该怎么做。

sentences.en: I'm sorry, sir.
sentences.zh: 抱歉，先生。

sentences.en: You didn't own headphones?
sentences.zh: 你没有耳机吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, but I had the kind like I'm wearing right now in the studio.
sentences.zh: 有，但我用的是我现在在录音室里戴的那种。

sentences.en: Like these big over-ear?
sentences.zh: 那种大的耳罩式耳机？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: This is what people wear to the gym when they want to lift weights, though.
sentences.zh: 不过那是人们去健身房举重时戴的。

sentences.en: Yeah, I couldn't see taking these out outside and like holding the phone and yeah, I didn't really think that through.
sentences.zh: 是的，我没法想象戴着这些出门，还要拿着手机，是的，我没怎么考虑过这一点。

sentences.en: I just think most people are going to be like, the music critic didn't listen to it.
sentences.zh: 我只是觉得大多数人会说，这位乐评人居然没听音乐。

sentences.en: to music when he was running?
sentences.zh: 跑步的时候没听音乐？

sentences.en: No, it was a way to empty my head, I suppose, and get me in a kind of mental position to begin writing when I got home.
sentences.zh: 不，我想这是一种清空大脑的方式，让我进入一种心理状态，以便回家后开始写作。

sentences.en: And then something changed for you, so tell me about that.
sentences.zh: 然后情况对你来说发生了变化，跟我说说那个吧。

sentences.en: So then the pandemic came and time got all weird.
sentences.zh: 后来疫情来了，时间变得很奇怪。

sentences.en: I could run in the middle of the street in the Bronx and I went running for much longer times and I remember going out running one day, listening to music and coming back
sentences.zh: 我可以在布朗克斯区的街道中间跑步，我跑的时间长多了，我记得有一天出去跑步，听着音乐回来，

sentences.en: and thinking,
sentences.zh: 然后心想，

sentences.en: I think I've just listened better than I've ever listened in my life.
sentences.zh: 我想我刚刚听到了我一生中最好的音乐。

sentences.en: It was a weird feeling.
sentences.zh: 那是一种奇怪的感觉。

sentences.en: I felt like something had happened.
sentences.zh: 我觉得发生了什么事。

sentences.en: What were you listening to?
sentences.zh: 你在听什么？

sentences.en: I wish I could remember.
sentences.zh: 我真希望我能记得。

sentences.en: Oh no!
sentences.zh: 噢，不！

sentences.en: Yeah, I know, I wish I could remember.
sentences.zh: 是的，我知道，我真希望我能记得。

sentences.en: But you said you felt like something had happened.
sentences.zh: 但你说你觉得发生了什么事。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So what happened?
sentences.zh: 那么发生了什么？

sentences.en: What changed?
sentences.zh: 什么改变了？

sentences.en: The easiest way to put it is that I think most people when they listen to music as they run, they're listening to music in order to be a better runner.
sentences.zh: 最简单的说法是，我认为大多数人在跑步时听音乐，是为了成为更好的跑者。

sentences.en: In other words, they're listening to music to set a pace, certain tempo, or maybe to pump themselves up or take their mind off of things or take their mind off the fact
sentences.zh: 换句话说，他们听音乐是为了设定节奏、特定的速度，或者可能是为了给自己打气，或者转移注意力，或者不去想

sentences.en: that they don't really like running or whatever.
sentences.zh: 他们其实不喜欢跑步之类的事实。

sentences.en: And I guess I thought, well, what if you turn that around and you run so that you could be a better listener?
sentences.zh: 我想我当时想，如果反过来呢？你跑步是为了成为更好的听众？

sentences.en: What does that mean?
sentences.zh: 那是什么意思？

sentences.en: What happened to you that you thought that on this run?
sentences.zh: 在那次跑步中，你发生了什么让你产生这种想法？

sentences.en: I realized that I could actually run into the heart of the music itself.
sentences.zh: 我意识到我真的可以跑进音乐的核心。

sentences.en: And that running could be a way of taking the measure of music in a way that I really hadn't done before.
sentences.zh: 跑步可以成为一种衡量音乐的方式，这是我以前从未做过的。

sentences.en: So I started just in my own mind, I started calling this running a song.
sentences.zh: 所以我开始在脑海里把这称为“跑一首歌”。

sentences.en: Like, if I found a song interesting in any way, the next thing for me to do would be to run it and see how it felt.
sentences.zh: 比如，如果我觉得一首歌在任何方面很有趣，我接下来的做法就是跑着听它，看看感觉如何。

sentences.en: So music was not just about music anymore.
sentences.zh: 所以音乐不再仅仅是音乐了。

sentences.en: Music was about place and music was about motion.
sentences.zh: 音乐关乎空间，音乐关乎运动。

sentences.en: I realize now that one thing about what running with music does for me is it essentially makes all music live music.
sentences.zh: 我现在意识到，跑步听音乐对我来说的一件事是，它本质上让所有的音乐都变成了现场音乐。

sentences.en: Like, whatever
sentences.zh: 就像，无论

sentences.en: I'm running to,
sentences.zh: 我跑着听什么，

sentences.en: it doesn't matter whether it was a live performance or not, it becomes one through the process of running with it.
sentences.zh: 它是否是现场表演并不重要，通过跑步的过程，它就变成了现场表演。

sentences.en: It, like, enlivens it.
sentences.zh: 它让音乐变得生动。

sentences.en: It turns the music into a sort of performance moment in which I am, you know,
sentences.zh: 它把音乐变成了一种表演时刻，在其中我，你知道，

sentences.en: I'm in there somewhere.
sentences.zh: 我在里面某个地方。

sentences.en: The experience that you're describing of, like, feeling that the music is in you and around you, you're in the world with it, it sort of reinvigorates the way that you are
sentences.zh: 你所描述的那种感觉，音乐在你体内和周围，你与它一起置身于世界中，这确实重振了你

sentences.en: hearing the music itself.
sentences.zh: 聆听音乐本身的方式。

sentences.en: Like, I'm wondering if that is a translatable experience other people could have when they put on their headphones and they go out for a run.
sentences.zh: 我在想，当其他人戴上耳机出去跑步时，这是否是一种可以转化的体验。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯哼。

sentences.en: I would say that increasingly these days, and this has something to do with earphones,
sentences.zh: 我想说，如今这种情况越来越多，这与耳机有关，

sentences.en: I mean, the fact that we are an earphone culture now, many of us treat music as a means to an end, essentially.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我们现在是一个耳机文化，我们许多人本质上把音乐视为一种手段。

sentences.en: Like, it's something that can help us accomplish something else that isn't really about music, per se.
sentences.zh: 就像，它能帮助我们完成其他与音乐本身无关的事情。

sentences.en: Like, it could help me with my workout.
sentences.zh: 比如，它可以帮助我锻炼。

sentences.en: It could help you with your workout, it could help the day go faster, it could set a pace, et cetera.
sentences.zh: 它可以帮助你锻炼，它可以让时间过得更快，它可以设定节奏，等等。

sentences.en: And what if music were not a means to an end?
sentences.zh: 如果音乐不是一种手段呢？

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: What if the music itself is actually what you want to be paying attention to?
sentences.zh: 如果音乐本身就是你真正想要关注的东西呢？

sentences.en: And then, what are you paying attention to?
sentences.zh: 那么，你到底在关注什么？

sentences.en: What should you be listening for?
sentences.zh: 你应该听什么？

sentences.en: Well, just to be fair, I do think a lot of people would say that they listen to music for the joy of listening to music, but I hear what you're saying as somebody
sentences.zh: 嗯，公平地说，我确实认为很多人会说他们听音乐是为了享受音乐的乐趣，但我作为一个

sentences.en: who listens to music to get herself through exercise, classes, including running,
sentences.zh: 听音乐来支撑自己完成锻炼课程（包括跑步）的人，我听懂了你说的关于为音乐而音乐的意思。

sentences.en: I hear what you're saying about music for music's sake.
sentences.zh: 我听懂了你说的关于为音乐而音乐的意思。

sentences.en: So I just sort of
sentences.zh: 所以我只是有点

sentences.en: what should I be listening for?
sentences.zh: 我应该听什么？

sentences.en: You could think about the music as a space,
sentences.zh: 你可以把音乐想象成一个空间，

sentences.en: and if it were a space,
sentences.zh: 如果它是一个空间，

sentences.en: what would you see in the space?
sentences.zh: 你会看到什么？

sentences.en: What's to the left?
sentences.zh: 左边是什么？

sentences.en: What's to the right?
sentences.zh: 右边是什么？

sentences.en: What's behind you, et cetera?
sentences.zh: 你身后是什么，等等？

sentences.en: You could think about what's at the bottom of this.
sentences.zh: 你可以思考一下这背后的基础是什么。

sentences.en: Is it drums?
sentences.zh: 是鼓声吗？

sentences.en: Is it singing?
sentences.zh: 是歌唱吗？

sentences.en: Or you could just think about what critics do, which is what is the essence of this thing?
sentences.zh: 或者你可以思考一下评论家们做的事情，那就是这个事物的本质是什么？

sentences.en: And that could be a sound, but it also could be an intention or a philosophy or something.
sentences.zh: 那可能是一种声音，但也可能是一种意图、一种哲学或其他什么。

sentences.en: Like, what is actually at the center of this enterprise such that if you took a pair of tweezers and extracted it, that the whole thing would fall apart?
sentences.zh: 比如，这个事业的核心到底是什么？如果用镊子把它取出来，整个东西就会分崩离析？

sentences.en: What is that?
sentences.zh: 那是什么？

sentences.en: And I think that pursuing that question is fun, and I think, you know, once you're really engaged in that question, I think you're listening to music as such rather than as a means
sentences.zh: 我认为追求那个问题很有趣，而且我认为，一旦你真正投入到那个问题中，我想你就是在听音乐本身，而不是把它当作一种

sentences.en: to an end.
sentences.zh: 手段。

sentences.en: I
sentences.zh: 我

sentences.en: wonder if you could give an example of a song that really came to life for you through this, or maybe even just a piece of music that maybe you understood better once you ran it?
sentences.zh: 想知道你能不能举一个通过这种方式真正变得鲜活的歌曲例子，或者甚至是一段你跑着听之后理解得更好的音乐？

sentences.en: Sure.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: This is a jazz record that I have listened to lots in my life, and the record is Eric Dolphy at the Five Spot.
sentences.zh: 这是一张我一生中听过很多次的爵士唱片，这张唱片是《Eric Dolphy at the Five Spot》。

sentences.en: And it was made in 1961.
sentences.zh: 而且它是1961年录制的。

sentences.en: It's a thrilling record.
sentences.zh: 这是一张令人激动的唱片。

sentences.en: It's a quintet, and each of these five members has a distinct personality, not unlike the
sentences.zh: 这是一个五重奏，这五位成员每个人都有独特的个性，就像

sentences.en: Beatles,
sentences.zh: 披头士乐队一样，

sentences.en: so that, you know, you feel this sense of, like, wow, completely different people here on stage, and they will often solo one after the other.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，你会感受到一种，比如，哇，舞台上的人完全不同，而且他们经常会接连进行独奏。

sentences.en: So it's this song called
sentences.zh: 所以这首歌叫

sentences.en: The Prophet,
sentences.zh: 《先知》，

sentences.en: written by
sentences.zh: 由

sentences.en: Eric Dolphy, and in The
sentences.zh: 埃里克·多尔菲创作，在《先知》中，你首先听到的是

sentences.en: Prophet, first you hear
sentences.zh: 埃里克·多尔菲的萨克斯独奏，

sentences.en: Eric Dolphy's saxophone solo,
sentences.zh: 然后你听到的是

sentences.en: then you hear
sentences.zh: 布克·利特尔的小号独奏，

sentences.en: Booker Little's trumpet solo,
sentences.zh: 接着你听到的是

sentences.en: and then you hear a piano solo by
sentences.zh: 马尔·沃尔德隆的钢琴独奏。

sentences.en: Mal Waldron.
sentences.zh: 而那正是让我一直没能真正理解的部分。

sentences.en: And that was the thing that I never really understood.
sentences.zh: 为什么？

sentences.en: Why?
sentences.zh: 你有什么不理解的？

sentences.en: What didn't you understand about it?
sentences.zh: 首先，它大约有四分钟长，所以篇幅不小。

sentences.en: First of all, it's about four minutes long, so it's sizable.
sentences.zh: 它总让我觉得有点晦涩。

sentences.en: It always felt kind of oblique.
